title: QBR Renewal Metric Playbook — Lab Notes
content:
Purpose and scope:
These are lab-style notes for the Customer Success QBR metric definitions we want to standardize for renewal conversations. Focused signals: request latency, service uptime (availability), cost per token (billable unit), and cache hit rate. This doc is intentionally informal — use it to drive the canonical spec in Confluence.

Audience:
- CS AEs and CSMs preparing renewal QBRs
- Solutions & Observability engineers supporting dashboards
- Product managers tracking product impact on renewal signals

High-level goals (quick):
- Make metric definitions unambiguous and reproducible from console/billing exports.
- Provide simple thresholds for red/yellow/green for renewal scoring.
- Give presentation-ready phrasing and two-slide templates per metric.

Metric 1 — Request latency (p50 / p95 / p99):
- Definition: time from request arrival at Redwood API ingress to first-byte of response delivered to the customer. Measured in ms. Excludes network client-side RTT; includes server processing, queuing, model compute, and streaming buffering until first byte.
- Why it matters: directly affects UX and user retention; correlates with perceived reliability.
- How we measure: use Redwood Console trace aggregator (ingress timestamp vs first-byte timestamp). Fall back to synthetic pings if no production traces.
- Formula: latency_pX = percentile(X, end_time - start_time) over last 30d business hours.
- Baseline sample numbers (example customer): p50=120ms, p95=480ms, p99=920ms.
- Suggested QBR targets (tiered):
  - Green: p95 < 500ms and p99 < 1s
  - Yellow: p95 between 500ms–1s or p99 between 1–2s
  - Red: p95 > 1s or p99 > 2s
- Owner: observability engineering for measurement; AE for customer narrative.
- Presentation note: show 30d heatmap + 7d trend line; annotate incidents that drove p99 spikes.

Metric 2 — Service uptime (availability / successful request ratio):
- Definition: fraction of requests that completed successfully (2xx or documented success contract) within SLA window. Expressed as percent uptime.
- Why it matters: renewal conversations hinge on reliability; legal SLAs often reference uptime.
- How we measure: daily rolling window of successful/total requests from Redwood logs; exclude scheduled maintenance windows (documented). Use both route-level and account-level aggregation.
- Formula: uptime_pct = 100 * (successful_requests / total_requests) over 30d
- SLA mapping examples: 99.9% (three nines) = ~43 min downtime/month.
- Suggested QBR thresholds:
  - Green: >= 99.9%
  - Yellow: 99.5% – 99.9%
  - Red: < 99.5%
- Owner: SRE + CSM for incident narratives.
- Note: For small-volume customers, supplement with synthetic checks to avoid noisy percentages.

Metric 3 — Cost per token (unit economics):
- Definition: realized cost to the customer per generated token (or per 1k tokens) as visible in billing exports after discounts and reserved capacity allocation. For internal renewal health, we prefer normalized cost-per-1k-token.
- Why it matters: renewals are sensitive to unit economics and predictable monthly spend.
- How we measure: derive from billing CSV: cost_per_1k = (billable_cost / billable_tokens) * 1000. Use last 30 days and prior 90-day trend. Adjust for committed discounts or reserved capacity avails.
- Measurement caveats: streaming partial tokens, rounding, and embeddings vs generation tokens should be separated.
- Suggested QBR thresholds (customer-dependent):
  - Green: stable or decreasing cost per 1k over last 90d (<= 5% variance)
  - Yellow: 5–15% upward drift without mitigation plan
  - Red: > 15% upward drift or unexpected invoice deltas
- Owner: finance ops + AE. CSM should own cost narrative in QBR.
- Presentation notes: include a small waterfall showing top contributors (model upgrades, higher token usage per session, longer contexts).

Metric 4 — Cache hit rate (prefix/KV cache):
- Definition: proportion of requests or tokens served using a cached prefix or KV lookup such that the model compute avoided full recompute. Expressed as percent.
- Why it matters: cache yields major cost and latency wins; high cache hit rate -> lower unit cost and faster p50.
- How we measure: Redwood runtime emits cache_hit, cache_lookup_count per request; compute hits / lookups over rolling 30d. Also capture effective token savings estimate.
- Formula: cache_hit_rate = 100 * sum(cache_hits) / sum(cache_lookups)
- Suggested QBR thresholds:
  - Green: cache_hit_rate >= 40% (depends on workload; some customers have 70%+ if many repeated prompts)
  - Yellow: 20–40%
  - Red: < 20%
- Owner: solutions engineering for optimization playbooks; instrumentation by runtime team.
- Remediation plays: prompt templating, shared prefix usage, deployment of cached rerankers.

KPI table (example — copy directly into slide):
Columns: Metric | Baseline (30d) | QBR target | 90d trend | Current color | Action required
Rows (sample numbers):
- Request latency (p95) | 480ms | <500ms | +10% | Green | Monitor; investigate 10/12 spike (model rollout)
- Uptime | 99.92% | >=99.9% | flat | Green | None; confirm maintenance windows logged
- Cost per 1k tokens | $4.20 | <= $4.00 | +12% | Yellow | Run cost-reduction playbook (quantize + batching)
- Cache hit rate | 18% | >=35% | -6% | Red | Solutions eng to propose prefix refactor by next sprint

Signal grading rubric (how CS should convert to renewal health):
- Green overall: all metrics green OR single yellow with concrete remediation plan and <5% MRR at risk.
- Watch: any metric yellow with no planned owner or >5% MRR at risk.
- Risk: any red metric AND customer impacted (tickets/incidents) OR >10% MRR at risk.

Presentation guidance for AE/CSMs:
- Start with the customer story: a 1-line impact statement (example: "Avg p95 latency dropped user task completion by 30% last quarter").
- Put the KPI table on slide 1, metrics drilldown on slide 2–3 with annotated incident callouts.
- Always include action owner and ETA for each yellow/red item.
- Keep the math simple: show sample invoice delta and the per-1k cost math; avoid runtime internals unless customer asks.

Data sources / dashboards to cite:
- Redwood Console: /observability/requests and billing export CSV
- Instrumentation: runtime logs (cache_hit, latency trace spans), SLI pipeline (prometheus -> long-term store)
- Billing: monthly CSV, committed usage report

Open questions / TODOs (short):
- Q: Should latency include streaming time-to-last-byte for streaming-heavy apps? (TODO: draft alternate definition for streaming flows)
- Q: How to normalize cost across dedicated vs hosted customers? (TODO: finance to provide normalization guide)
- Action: David to draft the Confluence canonical spec from these notes (due 2025-01-30).
- Action: Marta to validate cache_hit instrumentation on low-volume accounts (due 2025-02-07).

Appendix — quick formulas and commands (for Eng/SRE):
- sample SQL to compute p95 in traces table: SELECT percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY (end_ts-start_ts)) FROM traces WHERE org_id = X AND ts >= now() - interval '30 days';
- cost per 1k tokens in spreadsheet: = (sum(cost_column)/sum(tokens_column))*1000

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep this doc short; link to Confluence spec once finalized.
- Aim for 1 canonical slide template (KPI + one-liner + owner).
- Avoid duplicating existing CS playbooks; this should be metric-definition focused.

End of lab notes.
